title: Wooden ladders and a second driver: what the documents say
question: Do the documents contain a rule requiring wooden ladders, or a second driver at the back of a fire truck?
finding: No labor agreement mentions wooden ladders. Two Fire Department files do: the Strategic Plan (2017) names "wooden ladder repair and construction" as a Central Shops service, and 2016 Commission minutes record a wooden ladder raise at the 150th-anniversary event. The rear driver exists as the tiller operator: the firefighters' agreement pays tiller operators a 5% premium, the 2026 vacancy list shows 60 tiller positions on 20 trucks, and the words "second driver" appear in none of the 3133 documents.
how: Every text file in the download (3133, including 458 agreement texts) searched for the terms in each row; one Fire Department file (1 in all) was decoded from an unmapped font first. Position counts use the position codes on the vacancy list.
limits: 62 Board attachments and 131 Fire Department files are scans with no text and could not be searched; Fire Department general orders before 2026 and its equipment specifications are not on disk. The agreement provides crew size and operator pay, not the type of truck; whether a truck is a tiller truck is a Fire Department equipment decision the files on disk do not explain.

rows.question: Does any labor agreement require wooden ladders?
rows.finding: Not found in the 458 agreement text files searched (238 Board files: MOUs, CBAs, awards and amendments, clean, redline and draft), nor in the 300 Charter and code sections.

rows.question: Do wooden ladders appear anywhere in the documents? (2 of 3133 documents)
rows.finding: Fire Commission minutes (April 2016): a 65-foot wooden ladder raise demonstrated with antique apparatus at the Department's 150th anniversary event. Ceremonial, not a rule.
rows.quote: … will consist of hosting antique apparatus and demonstrating the 65 foot wooden ladder raise along with a host of other events taking place that morning. …

rows.question: Do wooden ladders appear anywhere in the documents? (2 of 3133 documents)
rows.finding: Fire Department Strategic Plan (November 2017): names wooden ladder repair and construction among the services Central Shops (General Services Agency) provides to the Bureau of Equipment. A planning document, not an agreement or a rule.
rows.quote: … Equipment – The Department’s Bureau of Equipment works closely with Central Shops, relying on them for such services as wooden ladder repair and construction, vehicle …

rows.question: What else do the Fire Department files say about the ladder shop?
rows.finding: Fire Commission minutes (August 2017) record a commissioner's tour of the ladder shop; the material is not stated.
rows.quote: took a tour of the ladder shop and was fascinated to see how the ladders are built and she was wondering if the ladder team …

rows.question: What do the agreements say about ladders at all?
rows.finding: Only aerial (truck-mounted) ladders: the City pays to test and recertify them (section 39.1), and a truck whose aerial ladder is out of service carries a sixth member (section 22.1c). Neither names a material.
rows.quote: The City agrees to pay for the inspection, testing, and recertification of the structural integrity and safety of all frontline and relief SFFD aerial …

rows.question: Is "fiberglass" mentioned?
rows.finding: Not found in the 3133 documents searched.

rows.question: Is "aluminum ladder" mentioned?
rows.finding: Not found in the 3133 documents searched.

rows.question: Does any document use the words "second driver" or "rear driver"?
rows.finding: Not found in the 3133 documents searched.

rows.example: Second driver at the back of a fire truck
rows.question: Is the rear steering position (tiller operator) in the firefighters' agreement?
rows.finding: Yes. "Tiller" appears in 45 of the 3133 documents, 20 of them agreement texts. The Unit 1 agreement pays tiller operators the 5% apparatus operator premium; the first full agreement text on disk with it is from 2018. The agreement sets crew size (one officer and four firefighters per truck), not which trucks must be tiller trucks.
rows.quote: Employees assigned to perform the duties of apparatus operator (pump operator, aerial truck operator, tiller operator, Rescue Squad driver, Bureau of Equipment driver, Service …

rows.example: Second driver at the back of a fire truck
rows.question: How does the Controller describe a truck crew?
rows.finding: The 2004 review lists a driver and a separate tiller among the five on each truck.
rows.quote: Trucks are staffed with one officer (H20 lieutenant or H30 captain), one driver (H2), one tiller (H2), one EMT (H2), and one firefighter (H2).

rows.example: Second driver at the back of a fire truck
rows.question: How many tiller positions are there now?
rows.finding: The Fire Department vacancy list (General Order 26 A-071, 2026) shows 60 tiller-operator positions on 20 trucks and 60 truck-driver positions (counted by position code; names not used).
rows.quote: Vacancy bidding for Firefighters (H-2), Firefighter/Paramedics (H-3 Level 3), Incident Support Specialists (H-10), Field Rescue Captains (H33), Officers (H20 & H30), and Battalion Chiefs (H40) …

rows.example: Second driver at the back of a fire truck
rows.question: Does the Charter name the position?
rows.finding: Charter A8.405 lists "tillermen" among the fire ranks whose pay is set by survey of other large California cities.
rows.quote: … substantially the duties being performed on the effective date of this section by drivers, stokers, tillermen, truckmen, or hosemen, in the San Francisco Fire Department. …

rows.example: Second driver at the back of a fire truck
rows.question: Has any official review questioned the tiller position?
rows.finding: Not found in the 22 official reviews on disk or in the 2014 Budget and Legislative Analyst audit. The Controller (2004) compared truck crew sizes, not the tiller.

sources.t: San Francisco Fire Department: Strategic Plan, November 2017
Board of Supervisors: labor agreement texts attached to the Board files that adopted them (Legistar)
San Francisco Fire Department: General Orders, 2026 (vacancy list, General Order 26 A-071)
Controller: A Review of the San Francisco Fire-EMS System, April 2004
